def peek(seq):
    """ Retrieve the next element of a sequence

    Returns the first element and an iterable equivalent to the original
    sequence, still having the element retrieved.

    >>> seq = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
    >>> first, seq = peek(seq)
    >>> first
    0
    >>> list(seq)
    [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
    """
    iterator = iter(seq)
    item = next(iterator)
    return item, itertools.chain([item], iterator)


def peekn(n, seq):
    """ Retrieve the first n elements of a sequence.

    Yields the first n items from the input iterable, consuming them
    from the input iterator. If the input has fewer than n items,
    yields all available items.

    >>> list(peekn(3, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]))
    [0, 1, 2]
    >>> list(peekn(10, [0, 1]))
    [0, 1]
    """
    it = iter(seq)
    for i in range(n):
        try:
            yield next(it)
        except StopIteration:
            return
